scope: All 28 D12 clauses, one U operational obligation and 40 proposed case actions/expectations reviewed against all 77 retained primary-text blocks; partial documentary scope only. No runtime or whole-Session closure. Focused comparison with the concurrently authored Clip View metadata owner also checks canonical ownership; it is not a full Clip View review.

semantic_review.clauses_001_010: Launch/stop/deactivation contexts, double Stop, metadata, grid/group slots, one-clip relation, width and scene cancellation follow primary text. Pending launch must be independently observed; timing/rollback and signal properties remain U.
semantic_review.clauses_011_013: Next-scene On selects the following row; Off disables that automatic rule without inventing preservation of prior selection. Scene metadata/order and positional numbering are documentary. Ctrl/Ctrl+arrow in source are retained as written; no unconditional Cmd substitution.
semantic_review.clauses_014_020: Scene tempo/meter UI and manual domains remain D12 with target-U, not replacements for T1 transport/storage laws. Reset sentinels, boundaries, keyboard contexts and target constructor defaults remain unknown. Pre-Live11 migration input is expressly a future prerequisite.
semantic_review.clauses_021_025: Track Status modes and import layout follow text without display/timing/codec claims. Select on Launch remains separate from Select Next Scene on Launch. Removed-stop branch is a null-comparator signal obligation; empty armed recording is left to its owner.
semantic_review.clauses_026_028: Capture copies/runs scenes as a visible-state proposal; no-interruption output has no supplied signal oracle. Transfer order is an attempt with unknown ties/overlaps; image glyphs are not invented. Consolidate scene/clip/file conditions retain Arrangement signal/destination ownership.
semantic_review.compound_requirements: Spec/research explicitly require extra per-branch cases before closure; single catalog rows do not silently close every mode, group configuration, gesture, migration or lifecycle branch.
semantic_review.canonical_boundaries: Recording REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-031 retains scene-name tempo/meter qualifier; Arrangement 009/010/020/021 and existing launch/playback/transport ownership are linked without new signal/scheduler laws. One narrow metadata-ownership overlap remains: Session REQ004 and Clip View REQ004 both restate Session Edit/context Rename and Edit Info Text availability, rather than explicitly routing shared semantics to one owner.
semantic_review.clip_view_link: Resolved at review time; clip-view-workflows.md exists and explicitly assigns grid/scenes/transfers/selection-on-launch to this Session owner.
semantic_review.fixtures: No .als, raw audio/MIDI/Live Clip or pre-Live11 migration fixture is supplied. Independent active/nonmuted/nonzero positive baseline required for signal/no-effect/continuity claims.

findings.location: REQ-SESSION-VIEW-004 / SV-004; boundary with REQ-CLIP-VIEW-004 and REQ-CLIP-VIEW-005
findings.issue: The new Clip View metadata clause includes the same Session-grid Edit/context Rename and Edit Info Text actions as the Session metadata clause (CV:B019 versus SV-B015). The facts agree, but the current texts do not distinguish a Session entrypoint contract from the shared clip metadata owner, leaving two maintained canonical statements under the project one-canonical-fact rule. The overlap is not confined to separate title-bar versus Session contexts.
findings.requested: Narrow Session REQ004 to Session menu entrypoints/selection dispatch and explicitly reference the Clip View owner for shared Rename/annotation/color semantics. Preserve SV-B015 citation and SV-004 finite actions, and avoid broad rewrites or semantic changes. Retain the exact r1 manifest/payloads before a successor freeze. A clear view-specific entrypoint/reference distinction is sufficient.
